Great Food, Disappointing Service
Jul 2026 • Solo
First, I had the banana flower salad with chicken. It was fresh, and the vegetables were thinly sliced. The dressing was savory and gave the dish a bright, refreshing flavor. I felt that all the ingredients worked harmoniously together, and the combination of textures made it enjoyable to eat. Next, I tried the prawn stewed in a claypot with starfruit. This was a comforting, home-style dish that really captured the essence of Vietnamese home cooking. The prawns were firm and juicy, while the sauce was rich, flavorful, and well-balanced. The starfruit blended naturally into the sauce. Overall, it was a very satisfying dish. Lastly, I had the lá lốt wrapped beef. Unfortunately, this was the weakest dish of the meal. The beef was overcooked, making it less tender than it should have been. It was also under-seasoned, so without the accompanying dipping sauce, it tasted bland. However, what disappointed me the most was the service. One of the dishes I ordered, sương sâm, was never served. I waited for 30 minutes before deciding to pay the bill and leave. I was surprised that a restaurant with so many staff members could overlook such a basic part of the dining experience.

Cuc Gach Quan offers a beautifully cosy and homely dining experience, with an atmosphere that immediately makes you feel comfortable and relaxed. The interior has a charming, lived-in feel that adds to the authenticity of the restaurant.

Cục Gạch Quán | Ho Chi Minh City
Mar 2025 • Family
Cục Gạch Quán is a lovely spot in Ho Chi Minh City that serves delicious Vietnamese food in a cozy, charming setting. The restaurant has a warm, homey feel with vintage decorations that make it really unique.

The menu features classic Vietnamese dishes, and everything I tried was amazing. The Bánh Xèo (crispy Vietnamese pancake) and Cơm Tấm (broken rice with grilled pork) were especially tasty. The flavors are fresh, authentic, and comforting.

The staff is friendly and attentive, making sure you feel welcome throughout your meal. The atmosphere is relaxed, perfect for a casual dinner or a gathering with friends.

If you’re in Ho Chi Minh City and want to try delicious, traditional Vietnamese food in a beautiful setting, Cục Gạch Quán is definitely worth a visit.

Authentic Vietnamese Cuisine
Mar 2024 • Friends
I' ve just had dinner last night at Cuc Gach.

Crab Spring Rolls: The shell is crispy, and the filling is fragrant with crab meat, mushrooms, and glass noodles. Must try this!!!
Chicken Salad with Ambarella Leaves: The chicken is fresh and sweet, complemented by the light sourness of ambarella leaves, making it very palatable.
Crispy Catfish with Green Mango: The catfish is crispy, enhanced by a sweet and sour sauce and green mango. The sauce deserves a 10/10.
Braised Pork with Eggs: The pork is tender and flavorful.
Sour Soup with Snakehead Fish: The broth is clear and delicious, flavored with dill and tomatoes.
Egg Fried Rice: The rice grains are firm yet soft and tasty.

Unfortunately, we were too full to order more.
The restaurant's interior is truly unique, reminiscent of a bygone era. The staff are extremely polite and professional.
Over a million VND for two people, the price is very reasonable.
If you want to experience authentic Vietnamese cuisine, this is the place to go.

I was invited to this restaurant not knowing what to expect, except that I had requested to eat sweet-and-sour shrimp soup, Canh Chua Tom Nau Bac Ha. I had no idea what was in store for me. The atmosphere, an avant-garde, modern take on traditional Vietnamese design (the owner is an architect) was thoroughly inviting, and I could not take it all in at once. I was not disappointed on any level, especially regarding the soup, which must be eaten with white or brown rice on the side.

The restaurant has numerous levels or floors, including private rooms and spaces, each more inviting than the others. At the Tan Dinh Quarter 1 location, there are actually two eating choices, each across the street from the other. I preferred the avant-garde choice, but the vintage French-Vietnamese option left nothing to dislike. It is there where Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt once had dinner, as the story goes.

Most importantly, the food is beyond expectation! As an American, I would call it farm-to-table eating. Fresh ingredients are brought in daily, and the multi-page menu (both English and Vietnamese versions) takes a good several minutes to digest--from meat to fish to noodles to rice to salads, etc. What is excellent, without doubt, is that the chef will cook any item you want in just the way you want. Cục Gạch Quán is, by far, the best eating experience I have had in HCMC over more than one visit. This time, I ate there on five different occasions.

Of course, there is the ubiquitous beer available throughout Vietnam, yet the wine selection (my preference) is also spectacular. There is a non-alcoholic lemon juice (actually, for me, lime juice) that is wonderful as well.

Finally, and most importantly, what makes Cục Gạch Quán special is the expertly friendly and kind staff. They can explain everything on the menu in Vietnamese, English, Japanese, and other languages, depending on the staff member. Everyone is welcomed, and no one feels left out.

This fall, a new location will open, but I find it difficult to imagine how this particular version of Cục Gạch Quán can be beat. I totally recommend penciling this restaurant on your itinerary.

One of the best dining experiences in recent memory
Nov 2016
My wife and I sought out Cuc Gach Quan based on a NY Times review. So many nice things to say about this spot.

Vibe
- Warm, homey setting but not overly casual whatsoever.
- It's put together and there's a lot of attention to detail. No surprise that an architect operates and designed the space.
- Traditional music plays over their vintage hi-fi system. They use a Pioneer CD player, even though I heard they spin vinyl. I'm actually more impressed by the CDs!
- The layout is pretty interesting. The bottom floor has 5 or 6 rooms that are partitioned, giving each one a distinct feel. They aren't closed off, so you can see what's happening in each of the others from any point of view. It makes the space feel cozy but still dynamic.
- Bathroom is adjacent to the fairly large indoor koi pond. Cloth towels are available rather than paper, something of which I'm personally a big fan.

Meal
- Menu is massive and the first page prefaces this before you dive in. It goes on and provides a thoughtful rationale and welcomes guests to ask the waitstaff for help.
- Ordered three dishes, all superb.
- Beef lemongrass soup: sour, hearty, topped off with fresh greens and spicy peppers. Sits somewhere between soup and stew and large enough to be a meal for one. Beef texture and shape was crumbly rather than sliced. Texture was surprisingly good and the beef very savory.
- Baby squid: Served in broth with lemongrass and onion. Certainly the more subtle of the three but equally tasty and complex.
- Soft shell crab: Blown away. Crabs are fried and coated in a sweet and sour glaze, topped with fresh sprouts and served over sautéed onions and peppers. Sprouts had that 'bite' that only really fresh ones have. The bellies of the crabs were plump and delicious.
- The portions were large, perhaps borderline huge. We had actually planned on those three being starters and we figured we'd then work our way up. The next round though, never happened - thoroughly stuffed.

Service
- Excellent. Friendly and consultative. Waitstaffs in Vietnam can be a bit complacent or frantic but here they were relaxed and in control.

Else
- Prices are incredibly reasonable. The plates combined cost $20 and the beer, wine, and scotch put the total at $40.

After a four-month stint living in Ho Chi Minh City and in spite of getting a bit "tired" of the Vietnamese staples of noodle/rice-based dishes, I decided to come here for my leaving dinner based on the great reviews and I am damn glad I did!

The first thing to point out is the location/decor. Though a great city, HCMC can also be a bit overwhelmingly noisy, so the fact that this is easy to get to as it is in the centre (D1), but tucked away in a back street away from all the noise pollution, gives it that peaceful, safe-haven edge. The restaurant itself is split into two - with one restaurant on either side of the road - but both have an awesomely rustic feel and are architecturally interesting with its different levels. Because of that, it's great place for a romantic quiet meal for two or for big groups.

Most importantly, the food was on point. There were seven of us and we shared three meat dishes (the beef lemongrass and caremelised pork were as mouthwatering as they sound), two massive rice bowls and two vegetable dishes as well as drinks and dessert. This scrumptious, filling, quality-tasting meal came to around 10 dollars each which is "pricey" for Vietnam, but worth every cent. It is also worth pointing out that the vegetables tasted particularly fresh and this restaurant is known for using preservative-free veggies, so this is also very suitable for any health-conscious person and/or vegetarian/vegan.

On a side note, the menu is bible-sized and can be a bit of a minefield so much so that there are even detailed instructions on the first page about how to use the menu! My advice would just be to ask the waiter/waitress for recommendations.

My other advice would be to just go, this place restored me back to being a Vietnamese food lover!

When a friend suggested we spend our Friday night dinner here (translation: Architect's House), I didn't think much of it - we loved Vietnamese food, and this place had good ratings.

I was ushered into a room through another stooped doorway and this room was filled with many tables. They gave me a menu in English and the main component of this restaurant is vegetables. The owner wants to cook them in such a way that you feel you are at his home - enjoying them the way he would cook them for his guests.

I eventually settled on one of my Vietnamese favourites - TOFU - with dried lemongrass and chilli. It was DIVINE! Their tofu is so so soft and flavoursome in Vietnam. Then i chose a standard fried rice with chicken which was huge (enough for two) and full of flavour.

There are many seafood dishes to choose from and if I ate seafood I would have tried one of these.

Full Cuc Gach Quan review: http://ivanteh-runningman.blogspot.sg/2015/07/cuc-gach-quan.html

With a name that means "Brick Restaurant", Cuc Gach Quan is a Vietnamese restaurant that specialises in home cooked, country style, traditional Vietnamese food, served in a French colonial setting. Founded in 2009 by Mr. Tran Binh, the architect-owner, alongside Ms. Tu-Tho Thai, Cuc Gach Quan is an ode to his grandmother's country home, an attractive mix of rustic nostalgia atmosphere, delicious authentic Vietnamese food, and excellent service. Little surprise that most visitors to Cuc Gach Quan rave about it, and it regularly makes lists of 'must-visit' restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam!

Ambience at Cuc Gach Quan (Dang Tat) is rustic, eclectic, and cozy. The beautifully restored French colonial building feels homely. The interior feels like a small museum, there's just so many things to see here! From the open kitchen, to the small pond in the middle of the house, the nostalgic movie equipment, the rustic wooden furniture, the colourful floor tiles, the retro artwork, the floors of varying heights, and all the small touches... Cuc Gach Quan is a visual feast for the eyes.

Service at Cuc Gach Quan (Dang Tat) is incredibly good, surpassing that of even the best fine dining restaurants. As a start, the staff here are educated in English, and the menu has English descriptions of each dish. Furthermore, staff are incredibly knowledgable on the extensive menu (with over 100 items!), and I highly recommend that you speak to them before ordering. They're able to make accurate and sound recommendations, based on your dietary requirements and even mood! Orders are fulfilled within 15 minutes, and empty / dirty tables are cleared quickly as well.

Food at Cuc Gach Quan (Dang Tat) is delicious. Focus is on fresh ingredients, prepared in traditional, country side style. Most popular Vietnamese dishes aren't on the menu, and you'll have to be open to trying new things. Taste in general is above average, not the best out there, but still very good. Cuc Gach Quan (Dang Tat) is more restaurant style, while Cuc Gach Quan (Thach Thi Thanh) is more casual, with a fixed menu. Portions are small, and it's recommended to order several dishes when visiting. Prices are reasonable for a restaurant, though more expensive than most places in Ho Chi Minh City, budget about VND ₫150,000 / SGD $10 per person for a meal here.

Honest review from a local foodie
Nov 2013 • Friends
If you are looking for a real AUTHENTIC Vietnamese meal, do not look further, it won’t disappoint you. 
I have tried many restaurants from high end down to street food vendor, this restaurant is on my top favorite. Why?

1.The origin & its mean: This restaurant is to serve home style meals that we, as Vietnamese somehow been forgotten along modernization and Westernization. You will find it “very old country style” with plain wooden chair, table, chipped bowls & plates. It’s Vietnam in 1960s, 1970s and years after we gained independence. As far as I know, the restaurant was dedicated to owner’s grandmother and beautiful memory of grandma’s meal in his childhood. 

2.The design: the restaurant is located in beautiful French colonial designed with lots of historic details like antique armoires, old vintage cassette, floating staircase… They are all given a lot of attention by owner. And if you don’t mind this restaurant will educate you not only about Vietnamese food but also Vietnam in the 1970s.

3. The staff: Boys & girls are very friendly and attentive. If you are lost in their thick and heavy menu, don’t be shy just ask them the best dishes and what you feel like, pork, beef or seafood. They will tell you all you need for a very delicious meal.

4. The food: Forget about frozen food and canned food. We eat fresh in Vietnam and “real fresh” in Cuc Gach Quan. The former Chef Bay (lucky me I met her once) told me the kitchen crew tries to make everything possible fresh from the scratch from the dressing sauce, cooking paste to things like tofu. Never tried egg-tofu? Please order. It’s fresh and will melt in your mouth. Another plus is that they have quite a number of vegetarian options and they can cook like what you ask. 

Most of dishes have lots of flavor or “extreme” flavor such as the one of shrimp brine or shrimp paste. If you are not familiar with strong smell sauce, stay away. Not forget to mention, I don’t eat salty food so my very first visit to Cuc Gach Quan was a bit of salty experience. If you are on low-salt diet, make sure you tell them less salt, lighter fish sauce. Everything else except that has always been great.

For you who are not sure what to order. Some of my favorite picks:

Appetizer: Mustard leaves rolled with pork, prawn, pickles and herbs (Cuon diep in Vietnamese) – MUST TRY!!!. Fresh rice paper roll (Goi cuon).

Main dish: deep fried egg tofu with lemon grass (Dau hut rung chien sa)- MUST TRY!!!
soft shell crab, braised pork with egg (Heo kho to), Egg- tofu stew with shiitake mushroom (dau hu kho nam), lotus stem, pork & prawn salad (Goi ngo sen tom thit), stir fired beef with lemon grass & chilli (Bo xao xa ot), Seafood spring rolls (Cha gio hai san), seafood fried rice (com chien hai san)

Some reviewers said the food was plain, nothing special...well I know it's all personal opinion and each of us have our own perception and preference. I hope you will find my review is helpful or at least you know what to order.

Love this one! It's quirky, bohemian and a bit avant-garde. Set in a restored French villa in an off the beaten track, it's definitely worth seeking out. Put on the map by being a favourite of Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie, the prices remain surprisingly affordable. The villa is divided up into different large rooms, each with characteristic funky Vietnamese decor. My favourite has to be the room at the top, approached via rickety steep stairs and complete with a sloping thatched roof. But the great attraction in that room is the main central table where the centre of a 4 poster brass bed has been cut out and a table inserted, and about 6 guest can sit in the adapted 4 poster bed to dine. The menu is very extensive and presented in an attractive menu book. The food, whilst not being fantastic, is very pleasant and the staff are friendly and professional. There is a good range of wines and freshly made fruit juices are very attractively presented in narrow glass bottles, stoppered with bamboo. 

Usually. as the dishes are not very big, we usually share dishes with friends and also order 2 extra, with enough rice for everyone. Our favourite dishes include the sweet and sour chicken as well as the chicken with lemongrass and chilies. The waiters will also happily bring you little side dishes of soy sauce with chopped up fiery red chilies, if asked for. However, for those not liking chicken on the bone in their dishes, it is worth knowing that some of the dishes, such as the sweet and sour chicken, are on the bone and not very appealing, so do check when ordering. However the chefs are happy to saute meat off the bone as an alternative, if requested. I can't comment on the sweet desserts as we have never had one, although occasionally we have ordered a plate of fruit, which is plentiful and delicious. 

This restaurant is a definite must to visit from time to time and a definite must for friends new to Vietnam who wish to sample Vietnamese cooking.

User-friendly access to homecooking quality Vietnamese food
Apr 2013 • Couples
This place is one of the best places to get proper exposure to the variety of Vietnamese homecooking in a pleasant, western-friendly environment.
Many of the dishes available, particularly with the variety of vegetables and diverse ways to prepare them (choice of sauteed, salad, soup, raw, etc), are exactly what my local family makes. And they taste almost - nobody cooks better than my aunt - as good, too. 
The number of dishes to choose from can be a bit of an overload and many are so "Vietnamese" that there isn't even a translation or explanation for the vegetable you're ordering. Hence, many people tend to stick to the usual: morning glory, pork, maybe even tofu (recommend fried with lemongrass and chili). However, I recommend trying out dishes like some of the sauteed flowers (e.g., courgette (thien ly) or squash (bi)) or tubers soups (khoai mo (purple yam)) as a first step to venturing off the beaten path. While I generally really enjoy the food at Cuc Gach, the only dish that didn't blow me away in my few visits was the sea bass in passion fruit sauce. The fish was a little dry on the inside and the sauce was a little sweet, and somewhat flat. Simply said, this dish is done better in other restaurants (e.g., May).
Aside from the obligatory beer, try one of the freshly squeezed juices. Granted, they may be a little sour - a tribute to the freshness, I suppose - but you can simply ask for more honey/sugar syrup to sweeten the experience. I would recommend pomelo or passion fruit.
Of course, the staff is only too happy to make recommendations of the right vegetable/meat combinations, if you indeed choose to go for a typical saute dish. In general, I found the staff to be very friendly and attentive without being overly submissive or overbearing. Command of the English language ranges from manageable to good, so that helps as well. Menus are available in both English, albeit with several holes as mentioned above, and Vietnamese. 
The decor is kept rustic with lots of wood. Tables made of old wood and pipes add to the rustic effect, only the chairs were a little ill-chosen by the architect owner (at least we were told by the staff that they were an architect). Tin can chopstick holders lend a certain flair of a Vietnam of days past. The mixture of A/C & non-A/C seating in this Villa-turned-Restaurant enables you to choose the right ambiance.
Of course, being considered one of the preferred dining choices among local expats and tourists, prices are comparatively high (sauteed vegetables = $4.50, large bowl of rice = $3). Regardless, this is probably one of the best places in the city to get proper exposure to a wide variety of authentic Vietnamese dishes in a western-friendly environment.
Overall, I would recommend this restaurant to anyone coming to visit and wanting to experience what I often eat at home with my family.

Unique setting, amazing food, impeccable service
Jan 2013 • Friends
Tucked away on a quiet side street in a residential neighborhood, Cuc Gach Quan offers a quiet oasis of excellent food served in a whimsical setting of antiques, artifacts and bric-a-brac. It's a bit of a tussle to find the District 1 eatery, but well worth the effort. The owner has made an honest effort to offer an authentic Vietnamese "countryside" dining experience as an antidote to the hustle and bustle of Ho Chi Minh's busy streets, and in the two visits I've made there the restaurant rates a solid 9 on 10. The emphasis is on quality, variety and authenticity, and every bite of every dish I've eaten at Cuc Gach Quan has been excellent. On our recent visit we went with stewed fish in a clay pot, where a salty/savory gravy envelops tender Mekong River fish, a delicious pomelo salad with fresh shrimp (a nice alternative to the usual overpowering dried shrimp), sautéed eggplant with onion, shrimp simmered with salt and chili (and finished with delicious fried garlic) and a bowl of fabulous red rice from the Mekong Delta. Meals for three, drinks and tip included, the tab came to just over $30. We were seated in a VIP room which featured interesting displays of cutlery and Vietnamese artifacts. The table was set with mismatched pottery, much of it cracked or chipped, which adds to the appeal of an authentic Vietnamese meal in a rural home. We put our trust into the friendly waitress, whose command of English allowed us to communicate our wishes for a genuine Vietnamese feast, and she rose to the challenge by suggesting the pungent pomelo salad to offset the saltiness of the fish dish. She was spot on with all of her recommendations. This is a "can't miss" fine food destination which is well worth the effort to find. Take some extra time to wander around the buildings, ponds and disparate dining rooms to get a full appreciation of the care and thought that went into creating a setting worthy of wonderful food.

Passion fruit and orange drink (served creatively in a bottle with a leafy stopper and straw from a type of water plant)

Soft shell crab
Sea bass
Tien Ly (lily flower) fried with garlic
Bean curd with lemongrass
Sour fish soup (to die for), although we were recommended the clam soup

Fish with Passion fruit
Pork ribs with Pineapple
Pumpkin soup
little cactus thingies - sorry I don't know the name but are reminiscent of Aloe and totally delicious

Drinks are great and include loads of cocktails and a variety of fresh juices. They have straws for the drinks made from the stem of the morning glory which is a great touch.

Very reasonable prices for the quality, I ate there last night and we had 8 or 10 dishes between 5 of us with several beers/wines/cocktails and we sat there for the best part of three hours and it came to just over 500,000VND each ($20-25 US).

Do yourself a favour and get there now!

Apr 2012 • Couples
This restaurant is extremely popular because Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt came to dine here...

This should be a reason to avoid this place at all costs, but... not so!

In a quiet back-street of District 3, this restaurant was created by an architect in a colonial villa: there are various settings, floors, ambiances, terraces, gardes, balconies... the restaurant itself is quite a labyrinth, and beautifully decorated. 

We shared a quite large array of dishes for two: all were very good (but not better than what you could get at other top-notch vietnamese restaurants in Saigon), some where truly outstanding.

We had;
Fried pork to roll in rice paper with vedges and herbs (similar to what you get elsewhere)
Fried tofu with ginger
A delicious vegetable I had never seen in my life (some kind of flower whos name I always forget).
A beef stir-fry
A oven-cooked fish
And the most oustanding dish:
A clam soup with dill. It had a lovely, spicy broth, giant clams, and the most unusual part, it was flavored with dill (aneth), which one usually associates with nordic, scandinavian cuisine, but that maybe the french imported to Vietnam, where its use was adopted and creaticely transformed, in the unique, idiosyncratic and super-tasty vietnamese way.... a real stunner!

We payed 1200000 VND for this garguant meal and wine, expensive for Vietnam standard, but definitevely worth-while.

So, go there, for the food, the setting, and the people, who flock here from all over Asia: Singapore, Taiwan, China, Thailand, definitely a good sign!

This restaurant is not recommended neither by Lonely Planet nor Frommer`s. But with so many positive opinions posted on Tripadvisor, we could not omit it during our stay in HCMC. 
The place is really superb. The driver from our hotel knew this place, so we arrived without any problems and it was great. Interesting interior / we were sitting on the first floor, with very narrow and steep stairs /, good, English speaking staff and, of course most important, excellent food. Do not miss the soft shell crabs - fantastic.

So worth the trip to this restaurant
This was by far the best food we had in Ho Chi Minh City. It is not located in the easiest place, but it is worth the trip. The street is not well known so make sure you look up the map on Google and draw the map or print it as taxi drivers are not very good at getting you there.
The service was great. Food was beautiful. We had a few dishes to share and liked all their dishes. TheirSoft shell crab is great, and we had this vegetable sauteed in garlic. It was a cactus type vegetable that there is no English name for. Do yourself a favour and try it. Wow. 
As for price, it is not the cheapest food, but still great price in Australian standards. We spent $30 AUS for both of us, but we tried a fair bit.
If you have a hard time choosing with the big menu, they can help you choose.
The venue itself is actually quite beautiful. Make sure you go to the toilet, just so you get to walk the platform over the water.
All in all, worth the visit.
